title: Our Story — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: The Director's message, the founding story behind Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools, our seal, and our Mission, Vision & the CLEVER Standard.
body: Discover Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools Faith and Scholarship, One Inheritance. A hybrid Islamic and secular institution in Ikorodu, Lagos State — built on the conviction that a child raised well in both faith and knowledge will want for neither, and named in honour of a father who believed exactly that. Read Our Story → Meet the Founder A Word From Our Founder The Conviction Behind the School Founder & Director Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi B.Sc. Applied Accounting (Oxford Brookes University) · M.Sc. Financial Management (Edinburgh Business School, Heriot-Watt University) · FCCA (UK) · FCA (ICAN) · Doctoral Candidate, Edgewood University, Madison, Wisconsin It is my privilege to welcome you to Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools — a hybrid Islamic and secular institution built in Ikorodu, Lagos State, on a single conviction: that faith and scholarship are not rival inheritances but one and the same, and that a child raised well in both will want for neither. As Director, I hold our staff and our institution to that standard in a school that is nurturing, secure, and genuinely inclusive. Two decades across banking, insurance, oil & gas, and consulting — in corporate reporting, taxation management, revenue generation, financial and business advisory, governance, and leadership — shaped how I think about building institutions meant to last. That same discipline is what led me to invest in schools whose only purpose is to educate. Our doors are open to Muslims and non-Muslims, to sons and daughters alike. Every educator on our staff is here to equip students with the knowledge, character, and practical skill a fast-changing world will genuinely ask of them. Whether you are considering us for the first time, already a parent in our community, or returning as one of our own alumni, you are welcome here. Our Story A Legacy Named in Honour of a Father Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools was founded by Zakariya Olanrewaju Anofi — a professional accountant and educationist — in July 2016. The school takes its name from the founder's late father, Anofi Aliu Akano — a clerk at the Nigerian Ports Authority whose own education was limited, but who was determined that his children would have the opportunities he didn't. Building the school became a way to honour that legacy after his father's passing, during a period when the founder and his younger brother were serving the nation during their NYSC year. The idea took shape years earlier, during Lagos Governor Babatunde Fashola's administration, and was carried through with the encouragement of the founder's mentor, Governor Seyi Makinde, his brother Lukman Olajide Anofi, and others. Rooted in the Imowonla community in Ikorodu, the school has grown into a byword for what focused, values-led education can do for an underserved area. 2016 Founded Named in honour of the founder's father. 2017 Rooted in Ikorodu Established in the Imowonla community, Lagos. 2020 Community First Humanitarian relief through the COVID-19 lockdown. 2021 Royal College The secondary college is established. 2023 Recognised Independently reported by Punch Newspapers. 2026 Five Institutions A fifth school and worldwide admissions. Scholarly Ties Abroad Grounded in Real Relationships SULTAN's Islamic and Qur'anic programme is grounded in real scholarly relationships, not built in isolation — visits like these connect the school to the wider community of Islamic scholarship its curriculum draws on. Beyond the classroom, the school extends its reach through free community lectures, humanitarian relief, and infrastructure support such as road maintenance and community electrification. Source: independent reporting by Punch Newspapers, August 2023. title: Academics — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Five institutions under one Board of Governors: the Nursery and Primary School, Royal College, School of Islamic and Arabic Studies, Qur'an College, and the Online & Distance Learning School. Compare them and find the right fit.
body: Academics · Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools One Standard. Five Institutions. A Lifetime of Learning. From a child's first morning in Nursery to the day a student earns an Ijāzah in the memorisation of the Qur'ān, every Sultan Hanafi institution is held to a single CLEVER standard — rigorous secular scholarship and deep Islamic formation, taught not side by side, but as one. Begin an Application → Compare the Institutions Our Academic Philosophy Faith and Scholarship, Held to One Standard A child raised well in both faith and scholarship will want for neither. That single conviction is the reason Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools exists — and the reason we refused to make families choose between a strong secular education and a serious Islamic one. So we built five institutions rather than one. Each carries its own age range, curriculum and learning model — a Nursery and Primary School, a secondary Royal College, a School of Islamic and Arabic Studies, a Qur'an College, and a new Online & Distance Learning School. What they share is more important than what separates them: one Board of Governors, one CLEVER standard, and a campus in Ikorodu, Lagos that welcomes Muslims and non-Muslims, sons and daughters, alike. The result is a continuous path. A family can begin with a two-year-old learning to read and to pray in the same week, and stay with us through examinations, memorisation of the Qur'ān, and beyond — never once stepping outside a community that holds academic excellence and Islamic character to the same, uncompromised measure. 0 Institutions One Board of Governors 0 Academic Departments at Royal College 0 National Curricula Nigerian & Saudi Arabian 0 Learning Stages Nursery to graduation 0 Established Ikorodu, Lagos State The CLEVER Standard One Standard, Held in Six Values CLEVER is not a slogan on a wall. It is the measure every teacher is held to, in all five of our institutions, from a two-year-old's first morning to the day a student receives their Ijāzah. Creativity We teach children to make, not only to memorise — entrepreneurship, technology and problem-solving woven into the timetable from the early years upward. Leadership Prefectships, competitions and service give students the chance to lead early — and the character formation to lead justly, as Islam asks of them. Engagement Small classes and known teachers mean a child is seen, not processed. Parents are partners, kept close to the life and progress of their children. Versatility Two national curricula, five institutions and flexible timetables let a family shape a path that fits their child — day or boarding, weekday or weekend, on campus or online. Ethics Daily Islamic character formation is not an add-on subject; it is the ground everything else is built on. Honesty, worship and adab are taught, modelled and expected. Reliability A verifiable credential system, a published calendar and a governance charter mean families can trust what the school says — and check it. A Continuous Journey From Age Two to Graduation — and Beyond Two day schools form the spine of a child's academic years. Three further institutions run alongside them, open at any age and to the wider community — so the journey never has to pause, and never has to leave. 2–5 Early Years First words and first prayers, in the same week. 6–10 Primary Literacy, numeracy and daily character formation. 10–18 Royal College WAEC/NECO across seven academic departments. Any age Islamic & Arabic Arabic mastery and the Islamic sciences, open to all. Any age Qur'an College Hifz to Ijāzah — day and boarding, 24–36 months. Anywhere Online & Distance The campus, extended to families across the world. The Five Institutions Every Age, One Family Each institution keeps its own character and calendar. title: The Curriculum Architecture — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: How our two adopted curricula, one CLEVER standard, and seven-stage learning pathway fit together across all five institutions — academic progression, character formation, leadership development, entrepreneurship, financial literacy, and Islamic formation.
body: Academic Architecture The Curriculum Architecture One educational model runs beneath all five institutions: two adopted curricula, one CLEVER standard, and a single continuous pathway a child can walk from age two through graduation. This page sets out how the pieces fit together — see each institution's own chapter for its subjects, timetable, and admission route. 0 Institutions 0 Adopted Curricula 0 Stages, One Journey Two Curricula, One Standard Basic School · Royal College The National Curriculum Programme The Basic School and Royal College both deliver the Nigerian National Curriculum, infused rather than diluted with entrepreneurial skills, financial intelligence, broad-based technology, personal development, career planning, and work-ready elective subjects. Royal College carries this across seven academic departments — JSS 1–3 through SSS 1–3 — and leads to BECE, WAEC, and NECO. See the Basic School's curriculum and Royal College's curriculum . Islamiyyah School · Qur'an College The Saudi Arabian Curriculum Programme Islamiyyah School and Qur'an College adopt the Saudi Arabian educational curriculum, with Saudi-approved textbooks and materials — Arabic language mastery, Qur'an and Hadith studies, and, for Qur'an College, the full Hifz and Ijazah pathway. See Islamiyyah School's curriculum and Qur'an College's curriculum . A full subject-by-subject syllabus, including specific textbook titles and publishers, is being prepared for publication here. See our Faculty Directory for the educators teaching these curricula today. Learning Pathways & Academic Progression From a toddler's first day in Nursery to a graduate stepping into university, every stage connects to the next — a single, deliberate pathway, not a series of disconnected years. Stage 1 · Ages 2–5 Nursery Where every child's journey begins — play-based learning woven with numeracy, literacy, and Islamic values from the very first day. Stage 2 · Ages 5–10 Primary National curriculum enriched with entrepreneurship, financial literacy, and digital fluency — the foundation for every pathway ahead. Stage 3 · Ages 10+ Sultan Hanafi Royal College A rigorous integrated curriculum across seven departments — JSS 1–3 and SSS 1–3 — where academic excellence, Islamic grounding, and modern pedagogy converge. Stage 4 · Ages 9–16 · Parallel Track Sultan Hanafi Qur'an College A full-immersion 24–36 month programme — complete memorisation of the Noble Qur'an, Tajwid, and the Sciences of the Qur'an, culminating in a certified Ijazah. Runs alongside Royal College, not after it, for students pursuing both. Stage 5 · Weekday & Weekend · Parallel Track Islamiyyah School Running alongside every other stage — carefully selected Saudi Arabian resources and SHRS-developed materials build authentic Islamic learning and structured Arabic language acquisition, open to the wider Muslim Ummah. Stage 6 · Every Year Group Leadership & Character Development Guided by the CLEVER framework and a structured student leadership pathway — from Student Representatives to School Prefects to Class Captains — every student is mentored to lead, not just to pass. Stage 7 · Beyond SHRS Graduation & Beyond BECE, WAEC, and NECO examinations mark the culmination of the Royal College years — opening the door to university and higher education, nationally and internationally. " Nursery → Primary → Royal College → Qur'an College → Islamiyyah School → Leadership & Character → Graduation — one ecosystem, walked by every Sultan Hanafi child. Every system below is real and live today; nothing here is a mockup. 0 Institutions Served 0 Portal Roles For Families Parent Portal Parent Portal A secure account for every guardian: submit and track an admissions enquiry, view your child's attendance, term results and fee status, receive school notifications, and complete a full institutional identity profile. title: Boarding Facility — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Full and half boarding for College & Qur'an memorisation students aged 9–16, in a home-like, supportive environment.
body: Student Life The Boarding Life Centre Discover a community where friendships flourish and memories are made. Our home-like boarding accommodation provides a comfortable environment in which boarders experience cordial relationships with roommates, creating a supportive and immersive learning environment. Boarders enjoy extra academic and extra-curricular support, more time to read and use a wide range of facilities, and the opportunity for self-reflection and discovery — including after-class Islamic lectures and post-Salah admonitions. Eligibility College & Qur'an memorisation students, ages 9–16 Full Boarding Monday to Sunday Half Boarding Monday to Friday Other arrangements Feasible by family schedule/budget Boarding Life The Dining Hall Boarders share meals together in a home-like dining setting, part of the daily rhythm of life on the boarding campus. A Day in Boarding Life The Daily Routine A structured schedule published to guardians, not left to vary informally — covering wake time, prayer, meals, study, memorisation, and rest. Wake & Fajr The boarding day begins before dawn, with wake time and the Fajr prayer. Morning Routine & Meals Preparation for the school day, followed by breakfast in the dining hall. Academic Day Full attendance at lessons alongside day students, with the same curriculum and teachers. Prayer Times & Meals The five daily prayers and mealtimes structure the afternoon and evening, observed together as a boarding house. Study Hours Supervised evening study, with extra academic support built into the boarding routine. Qur'an Memorisation & Muraja'ah Qur'an College boarders keep a dedicated memorisation and revision (Muraja'ah) session as part of the evening routine. Islamic Lectures & Admonitions After-class Islamic lectures and post-Salah admonitions, part of the reflective rhythm of boarding life. Free Time & Lights-Out Free time on the Recreation Ground or in the CCA Room, followed by a fixed lights-out with a logged room check. Supervision, Welfare & Safety Never Left Unsupervised From the Boarding Regulations (SD-04) Continuous Overnight Supervision Boarding supervision is continuous — there is no unsupervised overnight period, even during sleeping hours. A room check is conducted at lights-out and at least once more during the night, logged by name and time, with at least one warden awake and present in each boarding house overnight and a second reachable within the site. Safeguarding & Pastoral Care The Same Standard, Around the Clock The staff-student contact rules in the Child Protection & Safeguarding Policy apply in full to boarding staff. A new boarding student's first weeks receive additional pastoral check-ins beyond the standard routine, and any safety incident, illness beyond minor first aid, or substantive disciplinary matter is communicated to the guardian the same day. For Parents & Guardians Leave-Out & Staying Connected Leave-Out Authorisation Every Departure, Logged and Authorised A boarding student leaves the premises only with prior guardian authorisation, logged by the boarding warden. Guardians are entitled to request a call with the boarding warden within a reasonable response window — boarding is a partnership with the family, not a handover. Frequently Asked Questions Who is eligible to board? ▾ Boarding is available to Royal College and Qur'an College students aged 9 to 16. Full boarding runs Monday to Sunday; half boarding runs Monday to Friday. Other arrangements can be discussed with the school based on family schedule and budget. What's the difference between full and half boarding? ▾ Full boarding students remain on campus the whole week, including weekends. Half boarding students board Monday to Friday and return home for the weekend. Is a boarder ever left unsupervised overnight? ▾ No. Supervision is continuous, with room checks at lights-out and again during the night, and at least one warden awake in each boarding house at all times, per the Boarding Regulations

title: School Policies — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: Assessment, Anti-Bullying, Career, Dress Code, Equal Opportunity, First Aid, Health & Safety, Visitors, and Complaint policies, each prepared, reviewed, and approved by named office-holders.
body: Governance School Policies Every policy below is prepared by the VP Administration, reviewed by the Principal, and approved by the Head of Schools / Administrator, with a scheduled annual review. Print / Download as PDF 0 Published Policies 0 Governance Categories 0 Sections per Policy 0 School Founded Governance GV-01 Constitution & Governance Charter ❧ Policy Information Field Value Policy Code GV-01 Version 2.0 Policy Owner Board of Governors Approval Authority Board of Governors Review Cycle Biennial Introduction & Purpose This Charter states, in one place, what kind of institution SULTAN is, who governs it, and what each level of authority may and may not decide alone — the highest document in SULTAN's governance library, which every other policy sits beneath. Institutional Identity & Philosophy SULTAN is a single institution operating five distinct schools under one Board of Governors and one Management Team — not five independently governed schools sharing a brand. Authority flows from the Board downward through clearly delegated channels; Islamic scholarship and secular educational leadership sit together in the Management Team by design, a structural strength rather than something to flatten into a single generic role. Authority Structure The Board approves this Charter, all Tier 1 governance documents, and appoints the Head of Schools / Administrator. The Head of Schools / Administrator directs day-to-day operation across all five institutions. Each institution's Principal or Head Teacher holds academic and disciplinary authority within their institution, but may not adopt a policy that conflicts with a Board-approved document across all five institutions. Continuity & Governance Gaps When a named authority-role holder leaves, their authority passes to a confirmed successor or, until then, to their immediate superior — it never lapses or transfers informally. Where a role this Charter assumes is filled has no named holder (such as the Designated Safeguarding Lead today), that gap is tracked and reported to the Board until resolved, rather than left as a silent assumption. Conclusion This Charter does not establish SULTAN's legal corporate form, which requires confirmation from the school's own legal and corporate records, not an assumption made here. Retrofitted from the original v1.0 draft to SULTAN's full 13-section institutional standard (Policy Information, structured sign-off, cross-referenced governance detail). Prepared by Board of Governors Reviewed by Management Team Approved by Board of Governors (pending) Next review Upon adoption Academic AC-01 Assessment Policy ❧ Introduction At SULTAN, assessment is the process by which the quantity and quality of teaching and learning are measured through various techniques, and organised into interpretable forms across a number of variables. Objectives Evaluate teaching and learning practice against specific objectives. Give learners regular performance feedback and ownership of their learning. Give parents a clear idea of progress needed. Benchmark against local and national standards. Identify whole-school professional development needs. Ensure underperforming groups are identified for intervention. Enable educators to plan support to fill knowledge gaps. Uphold the school's high expectations and standards. Report clear information to management and the board of governors. Integrate assessment into planning and teaching. Forms & Techniques Forms: Diagnostic, Formative, Summative. Techniques: Oral questions, classwork, assignments, quizzes, project, test (POP/CBT), exams (POP/CBT). Feedback Learners get constant feedback. Parents receive broad sheets and oral feedback on Open Day each half term. Report cards issued at the end of every term. Report Card Components Learner's individual information and attendance record. title: Digital Qur'an Centre — Sultan Hanafi Royal Schools
description: What's real today toward a daily Qur'an companion, and the legally-clean path for the full Madinah-style reader.
body: Digital Qur'an Centre A Daily Qur'an Companion Our goal for this space: a student, parent, teacher, or ḥāfiẓ should be able to use SHRS as a daily Qur'an companion — not just a page of links. Here's exactly what that means today, and what a proper build requires next. The reader below is a first working draft, pending scholarly verification. Its Arabic text was transcribed by an AI from memory, not fetched from a licensed source (this environment cannot reach one — see below), and has not yet been checked against a printed Mushaf. The school has asked for this best-effort version and taken responsibility for verifying every ayah before it is treated as authoritative. Please do not rely on it for worship or teaching until that review is complete. Reader — Al-Fātiḥah & Surahs 93–114 The opening surah, plus the last block of the Qur'an — the portion most Muslim children memorise first and the one recited most often in daily prayer. The full 604-page Mushaf, verse-by-verse audio, and Hifz repeat-loop tools are a later phase (see below for why). What's Real Today, Beyond the Reader The Adhkār Centre Morning & Evening Adhkār with a Smart Tasbih Counter, Arabic recitation read aloud via text-to-speech, personal streaks, and achievement badges — fully built and live. See the Adhkār Centre . Qur'an College's Real Hifz Tracking Enrolled Qur'an College students already have a genuine Hifz & Ijazah tracker — per-juz' memorisation status, muraja'ah notes, and Ijazah progress — visible to their guardian in the Parent Portal. See Qur'an College and the Digital Campus . Today's Wird, on the Homepage A daily "Today's Adhkār" and "Today's Islamic Reminder" (a well-established verse or hadith, with its citation) greet every visitor on the homepage. See Today's Wird . Why the Reader Above Is Scoped and Unverified, and What Finishing It Needs Building the reader properly — the full 604-page Mushaf, verse-by-verse audio, and Hifz repeat-loop tools — means the verse text and audio need to come from a real, licensed data source fetched programmatically, then be checked by qualified reviewers before anyone relies on them. The version above is a deliberately smaller first step: 23 short, commonly-recited surahs, transcribed by AI at the school's explicit request and awaiting that same scholarly check. Research into what the fuller, licensed build needs: Researched Qur'an Text Tanzil Project 's Uthmani text is available under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 — verbatim copying and redistribution is permitted with attribution and a link back to tanzil.net. This is the standard source most Qur'an apps use. Researched Madinah-Style Typesetting The King Fahd Glorious Qur'an Printing Complex's own KFGQPC Uthmanic Script font is freely distributed for non-commercial typesetting use — this is how to get an authentic Madinah-Mushaf look. The scanned photographic pages of the actual Madinah Mushaf are a separate matter and are not under a comparably clear open licence — reproducing those specific page images would need direct written permission from the Complex first. Researched Recitation Audio Reciter audio hosted on sites like EveryAyah.com is generally under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial terms — usable for a non-commercial educational site like this one, with attribution, but each reciter's exact terms should be re-checked individually before enabling their voice specifically. Blocked, Not Skipped What Stopped This Build Going Further Today This working session has no outbound network access to Qur'an text/audio APIs (a sandboxing restriction, confirmed by testing), so the actual verse data for the fuller Mushaf could not be fetched from Tanzil and verified here, and audio recitation isn't wired in at all. The reader's navigation architecture (surah selection now; page/juz'/hizb, manual and auto-scroll modes, and Hifz repeat-loop controls next) is built to extend cleanly once a session with real network access, or the school's own developer, rep
